title: Why anti-Israel protestors are targeting New York’s anti-Zionist mayor
gist: Yglesias explains why pro-Palestinian activists heckled NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani at an October 7 vigil: they follow a left organizing playbook of picking winnable local fights (NYPD protest policing, replacing Commissioner Jessica Tisch) to build organizing capacity, though he thinks the approach is poor politics.

insights.claim: Mamdani is marginal to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in his actual responsibilities but central to its symbolic politics in the US as an uncompromising anti-Zionist mayor of the center of Jewish American life.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Explains why NYC governance becomes a proxy battleground for Middle East politics.

insights.claim: Activists target a sympathetic mayor over NYPD protest policing and demand he replace Jessica Tisch because a broad left theory holds that picking short-term fights drives more organizing when no short-term path to change US Israel policy exists.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Expect continued friction between Mamdani and the activist left, a political risk for NYC policing leadership.
insights.locator: Activists pick fights to drive more organizing

insights.claim: Dismissing the protests as dumb, as Mehdi Hasan does, is a mistake, even though targeting Mamdani is not a good way to do politics.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Reading the protests as strategic rather than irrational improves forecasts of their persistence.
